aramex smart. . ## The problem In 2019 about 86% of e-commerce orders in the Middle East were cash on delivery. That capped the market in three ways: E-tailers lost orders to failed deliveries, when buyers were not home or refused to pay at the door Aramex absorbed the cost of re-delivery and returns Consumers with thin credit files had no way to defer payment, so they paid upfront or put up with the friction at the door The insight Do not build a standalone BNPL that competes for attention. Embed credit in the delivery flow people already trust, use Aramex's delivery history as the underwriting data, and use Aramex's merchant network as distribution. That led to the one design decision everything else followed from: **the loan is created on delivery, not at checkout.** The consumer picks Aramex SMART at checkout, pays nothing, and the loan is born when the courier scans proof of delivery.

he consumer picks Aramex SMART at checkout, pays nothing, and the loan is born when the courier scans proof of delivery. It mirrors cash on delivery, with structured credit in place of cash. How a purchase works The consumer picks "Pay Later with Aramex SMART" at a partner e-tailer's checkout A real-time underwriting engine scores them against 20+ alternate parameters from Aramex delivery history and returns a decision with a personal credit limit in seconds The order is placed and the shipment is created, with no payment Proof of delivery triggers loan creation in the loan management system The repayment window opens, 14 days for Pay Later or the first instalment for Installments The consumer repays through the portal with PayPal, STC Pay, Telr or Apple Pay, depending on the market Six product components **Real-time underwriting engine:** Alternate-data credit decisions without bureau data, which was sparse in the region.

**Real-time underwriting engine:** Alternate-data credit decisions without bureau data, which was sparse in the region. It lifted approval rates by 45% against conventional scoring in the same segment. Thresholds and limit buckets were tuned with the Risk team as the portfolio matured **Consumer Portal:** Balance, due dates, full, partial and one-click repayment, custom pay-links for targeted collection, store credit and order history.

A separate mobile-first responsive build followed, with full Arabic right-to-left support **E-tailer widget and plug-ins:** An embeddable checkout widget plus self-service plug-ins for Magento, Shopify and WooCommerce, so non-technical merchants could switch it on with little developer time **Merchant Portal:** Orders, settlements, remittances, returns and self-service onboarding, which gave merchants transparency without a large support team **Leads Portal:** An internal tool that pre-loaded consumers with verified delivery histories before launch, so the product opened with a pre-screened user base instead of a cold start **Landing page:** English and Arabic from day one, with versions for Saudi Arabia and the UAE Four payment products **Pay Later (14-day):** The flagship, launched in Saudi Arabia at go-live in June 2020.

No interest if repaid on time **Pay in Installments (3x):** Three equal monthly instalments for larger orders, in Saudi Arabia and the UAE **Part Pay:** Pay a portion upfront or at delivery and defer the rest, piloted in the UAE **Prepaid:** A wallet model launched in Nigeria in December 2020, matched to a market where post-delivery credit was harder to run The COVID pivot In March 2020 the launch plan fell apart. It depended on physical merchant events, in-person activation and a broad category launch, and retail had shut.

The re-plan, executed on schedule: Moved the merchant launch to essential goods such as groceries, pharmacy and household items, where lockdown demand had spiked Switched to fully digital merchant onboarding using the self-service Merchant Portal already in development Made the underwriting engine more conservative on initial limits, with a plan to recalibrate as repayment data arrived Activated consumers by email and digital channels only, through the pre-seeded Leads Portal base Cut launch scope to the minimum live feature set and deferred the rest to the scale phase Aramex SMART went live in June 2020, six months from inception, with two e-tailers and a pre-seeded consumer base. The forced focus turned into a product insight: BNPL demand was strongest in high-frequency, necessity purchases, which shaped merchant priorities afterwards.

Rollout **Jun 2020:** Go-live in Saudi Arabia with 2 e-tailers **Jul to Oct 2020:** 25 e-tailers; PayPal, STC Pay and Apple Pay integrated **Nov 2020:** UAE launch with AED and USD support and the Telr gateway **Dec 2020:** Nigeria launch with the Prepaid model **Dec 2020 to Oct 2021:** Installments shipped, Part Pay piloted, responsive portal and the three e-commerce plug-ins delivered, merchant base growing toward 35+ Lessons **No bureau data meant the alternate-data engine was the plan, not the backup.** Getting the Risk team to trust delivery data as the main signal took pilot data and persistence **Trust was a design problem.** Mirroring the cash-on-delivery moment, with Arabic copy and clear repayment messaging, mattered more than feature depth **Merchant integration was the bottleneck.** The plug-in strategy removed it and made the jump from 2 to 35+ merchants possible **Three markets, one architecture.** Payment and currency logic had to be modular because each country had different rails, currency, regulation and behaviour Role Joined Finvolv in 2019 as Senior Product Manager and was the sole product owner on the Aramex engagement: product vision, flows and wireframes, design reviews and sign-offs with the visual design team, credit engine configuration with Risk, and delivery coordination with Engineering.
From December 2021 moved to Lead Product Manager across the wider Finvolv LMS while continuing to oversee the Aramex account.

X Bookmarks Architect. Description: Automating a Knowledge Ingestion Engine for a PM's Second Brain. Tech: Playwright, Python, Notion API, MCP, Warp Terminal. 🔍 The Problem PMs in Fintech and AI face a growing "black hole" of bookmarks on X—thousands of saved posts that remain unsorted, disconnected from workflows, and effectively useless for knowledge retrieval. I had **2,000+ bookmarks** accumulated over years. Finding anything meant endless scrolling.

The knowledge was there, but completely inaccessible. 💡 The Solution Built an end-to-end data pipeline to extract, process, and ingest all bookmarks into a structured Notion "Second Brain" with **zero manual effort**. 🛠️ Implementation Steps 🔐 Authentication & Harvesting (Playwright) Automated browser session with cookie-based authentication Handled X's anti-bot measures with realistic interaction patterns Session persistence for reliable multi-hour extractions 📜 Infinite Scroll Engineering Custom scroll algorithm to handle X's lazy-loading Implemented backoff strategies to avoid rate limits Checkpoint system to resume interrupted sessions ⚡ Zero-Token Sync Engine Direct Notion API integration via MCP (Model Context Protocol) Structured data mapping: URL, text, author, timestamp, categories 95% reduction in API costs vs standard AI processing approaches 🎯 Algorithmic Noise Filtering Rule-based filtering to exclude sports, memes, and off-topic content Category auto-assignment based on content patterns Priority scoring for fintech/AI/product content 📊 Technical Highlights | Metric | Result | |:-------|:-------| | 📦 Items Migrated | **2,000+** | | 💰 API Cost Reduction | **95%** vs AI-based approaches | | 🤖 Manual Effort | **Zero** post-setup | | ✅ Success Rate | **99.2%** | 🎯 Why This Matters for PMs This project demonstrates: 💻 **Technical Literacy:** Writing production code, not just specs 📈 **Scalable Workflows:** Building systems that compound over time 🔗 **Tool Integration:** Connecting disparate tools into cohesive pipelines 🧩 **Problem-Solution Fit:** Identifying personal pain points and engineering solutions 🔧 Stack **Playwright (Python):** Browser automation and scraping **Warp Terminal:** Modern terminal for development **Notion API + MCP:** Structured knowledge base integration **Python 3.x:** Core scripting and data processing

Custom MCP for Lenny's Podcast. Description: Building a Product Intelligence Server for elite PM frameworks. Tech: Python, MCP SDK, Claude Code, Markdown. 🔍 The Problem PM frameworks are trapped in transcripts. The best product advice from interviews with top PMs—pricing strategies, growth tactics, roadmap frameworks—sits buried in hours of podcast content. Context-switching between IDE and browser to find relevant advice slows down technical drafting.

Every time I'm writing a PRD or strategy doc, I'd think "Lenny had a great episode on this..." and lose 20 minutes searching. 💡 The Solution A custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that indexes **320+ Lenny's Podcast transcripts**, allowing an AI agent to search for elite PM advice in real-time—directly from my IDE. 🛠️ Technical Implementation 📥 Data Acquisition Cloned 320+ markdown transcripts from ChatPRD's public archive Organized by guest, topic, and date for efficient indexing 2M+ words of PM wisdom, locally accessible 🖥️ MCP Server Development Built Python-based server using the official MCP SDK Implemented semantic search across all transcripts Handles concurrent queries with low latency 🔧 Custom Tool: search_lenny_insights Query interface: natural language questions about PM topics Returns relevant excerpts with episode context Supports filtering by guest, topic, or date range 🤖 Claude Code Integration Connected via --mcp flag for agentic workflows Real-time access during PRD drafting No browser context-switching required 💬 Example Usage **Query:** "What does Shreyas Doshi say about high-agency PMs?" **Response:** Found 3 relevant excerpts from Shreyas Doshi episodes discussing how high-agency PMs don't wait for permission—they identify the most important problem and start solving it. 📊 Impact | Metric | Result | |:-------|:-------| | 📚 Transcripts Indexed | **320+** | | 📝 Total Content | **2M+ words** | | ⚡ Search Latency | **Under 2s** | | 🎯 Context Switches Saved | **100%** | 🎯 Why This Matters Transformed a static archive into an **active tool** for: 📄 Writing PRDs with real framework references 🧠 Brainstorming technical strategy with expert backing 📈 Learning PM craft through targeted retrieval ⚡ Building "just-in-time" knowledge systems 🌐 The Bigger Picture This project demonstrates the power of MCP for building personal productivity tools.

Any knowledge corpus—books, courses, internal docs—can become an AI-accessible resource with the same pattern. 🔧 Stack **Python:** Core server implementation **MCP SDK:** Model Context Protocol framework **Claude Code:** AI agent integration **Markdown:** Transcript storage format

chunks.text: Nano Platformer. Description: A 12-Stage 2D Platformer Game with Upgrades, Boss Fights & Adaptive Difficulty. Tech: Python, Pygame, JSON, Sprite Animation. 🔍 The Problem Wanted to build a **complete game from scratch**—not a tutorial clone, but a fully-featured platformer with real game design: progression systems, enemy AI, boss fights, and player-driven difficulty. The goal was to learn game development fundamentals by shipping something end-to-end: physics, state machines, animation, game balance, and persistence. 💡 The Solution A 12-stage 2D platformer with a full campaign arc: escalating enemy types, a shop/upgrade system, a multi-phase boss fight, and an adaptive assist system that adjusts difficulty based on player performance.
ade system, a multi-phase boss fight, and an adaptive assist system that adjusts difficulty based on player performance.

Built entirely in Python with Pygame—no game engine, no shortcuts. 🛠️ Technical Implementation ⚙️ Physics Engine Custom gravity and acceleration system with configurable constants AABB collision detection for platforms, walls, and entities Jump mechanics with variable height (tap vs hold) for precise control Friction and air resistance for natural-feeling movement 👾 Enemy AI System **Walkers:** Patrol paths with edge detection and turn behavior **Shooters:** Ranged enemies with projectile spawning and cooldown timers **Boss:** Multi-phase fight with burst-fire patterns, health thresholds, and enrage mechanics State machine architecture for clean AI behavior transitions 🛒 Upgrade System **Vitality:** Max HP increases and passive health regen **Blade:** Damage multiplier and attack range extensions **Tempo:** Movement speed and jump height boosts 3 tiers per upgrade path, purchased with in-game currency from defeated enemies 🎚️ Adaptive Difficulty Tracks player deaths per stage and cumulative performance Activates assist mode after repeated failures: extra HP, damage reduction, extended checkpoints Scales back assistance when player improves—never feels patronizing 📁 JSON-Based Level System Each stage defined as a JSON file: platforms, enemy spawns, collectibles, and triggers Hot-reloadable during development for rapid level design iteration Supports custom tilesets and background layers per stage 💾 Persistent Save System Player progress, upgrades, and currency saved to local JSON Checkpoint system within stages for respawn on death Full campaign state preserved across sessions 🗺️ Campaign & Boss Fights 🎯 Key Features 🎮 **12-Level Campaign:** Progressive difficulty from tutorial to boss fight 👾 **3 Enemy Types + Boss:** Walkers, shooters, and a multi-phase boss encounter 🛒 **Shop & Upgrades:** 3 upgrade paths (Vitality/Blade/Tempo) with 3 tiers each 🎚️ **Adaptive Assist:** Dynamic difficulty adjustment based on player performance ✅ **Checkpoint/Respawn:** Mid-stage checkpoints with instant respawn 🎨 **Sprite Animation:** AI-generated character and environment assets with frame-by-frame animation 💾 **Persistent Save:** Full progress saved across sessions 📊 Technical Highlights | Metric | Detail | |:-------|:-------| | 🎮 Campaign Stages | **12** | | 👾 Enemy Types | **3 + Boss** (Walker, Shooter, Boss) | | 🛒 Upgrade Paths | **3** (Vitality, Blade, Tempo) | | 🎚️ Upgrade Tiers | **3 per path** (9 total) | | 💾 Save Format | **JSON** (portable, human-readable) | | 🖼️ Art Pipeline | **AI-generated** sprites + manual cleanup Voice Journal. Description: AI-Powered Voice-to-Text Journaling App with Transcription, Summaries & Weekly Insights. Tech: React Native, Expo, SQLite, OpenAI Whisper, GPT-4o-mini, TypeScript. 🔍 The Problem Journaling is powerful, but **typing on a phone kills the flow**. Thoughts come fastest when you're walking, commuting, or lying in bed, moments when a keyboard is the last thing you want. Voice memos solve the capture problem but create a new one: recordings pile up, unsearchable and unreviewed. You end up with hundreds of audio files and zero actionable insights. 💡 The Solution A mobile-first voice journal that turns speech into structured, searchable entries through an AI pipeline: **Record → Transcribe → Summarize → Tag → Analyze**.

Every entry gets an AI-generated summary, mood tag, and topic classification, making weeks of thoughts instantly searchable and reviewable through weekly insight reports. 🛠️ Technical Implementation 🎙️ Recording Engine Built on Expo AV for cross-platform audio capture Pause/resume support for natural, unstructured thoughts Background recording with lock-screen controls Configurable audio quality and format settings 🧠 AI Processing Pipeline **Step 1 - Transcription:** OpenAI Whisper API converts audio to text with high accuracy **Step 2 - Summarization:** GPT-4o-mini condenses transcripts into concise journal entries **Step 3 - Auto-Tagging:** AI extracts topics, people, and themes from content **Step 4 - Mood Detection:** Sentiment analysis classifies emotional tone per entry 💾 SQLite Schema & Migrations Normalized schema: entries, tags, entry_tags, weekly_summaries Version-tracked migrations for safe schema evolution Full-text search index on transcripts and summaries Efficient pagination for large journal histories 🔐 Privacy & Security Biometric authentication (Face ID / fingerprint) on app launch All data stored locally on-device via SQLite Audio files encrypted at rest Zero cloud dependency, no account required 🎯 Key Features 🎙️ **Voice Recording:** Tap-to-record with pause/resume and waveform visualization 📝 **AI Transcription:** Whisper-powered speech-to-text with punctuation and formatting 📋 **Smart Summaries:** GPT-4o-mini distills rambling thoughts into clear entries 🏷️ **Auto-Tagging:** Topics, people, and themes extracted automatically 😊 **Mood Detection:** Emotional tone tracked across entries for pattern recognition 🔍 **Full-Text Search:** Find any thought by keyword across all entries 📊 **Weekly Insights:** AI-generated analytics on mood trends, top topics, and journaling streaks 📴 **Offline-First:** Works without internet; Why Your Home Loan Isn't Really 'Yours'. Tags: Lending, Home Loans, RBI. Excerpt: Understanding the complex ownership structures behind your housing loan and what it means for borrowers. When you take a home loan, you assume the bank that approved it will service it throughout. But the reality of modern lending is far more complex. The Hidden Journey of Your Loan Your home loan might travel through multiple institutions during its lifetime: **Origination** - The lender who approves your loan **Servicing** - The entity collecting your EMIs **Ownership** - The actual holder of your debt These can be three different entities. Why This Matters Understanding loan ownership helps you: Know who to contact for issues Understand why terms might change Navigate prepayment and foreclosure Protect yourself during disputes The Co-Lending Angle With RBI's co-lending guidelines, this complexity is increasing.

chunks.text: Implementing RBI's Co lending Directions. Tags: Co-lending, RBI, Technical. Excerpt: A technical deep-dive into building co-lending systems that comply with RBI's regulatory framework. Co-lending is one of the most significant regulatory innovations in Indian lending. Here's how to build systems that work.

Understanding Co-lending RBI's co-lending model allows banks and NBFCs to jointly originate loans: **Bank share:** Minimum 20% of the loan **NBFC share:** Maximum 80% of the loan **Risk sharing:** Proportional to contribution Technical Architecture Considerations Loan Origination Single application, dual underwriting Unified customer experience Split disbursement handling Servicing Complexity Single EMI collection Proportional distribution Unified customer communication Default Management NPA recognition alignment Collection coordination Recovery sharing Key Implementation Challenges **Data synchronization** between bank and NBFC systems **Reconciliation** of daily transactions **Regulatory reporting** for both entities **Customer service** coordination Our Approach at M2P We built the co-lending orchestration module to handle: Real-time loan allocation Automated compliance checks Unified servicing layer Transparent reporting Results 5 enterprise accounts onboarded $50M+ loan volume processed Zero compliance issues
